transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-21 16:00 PST
Duration: 43 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Eliot Zhang (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (CTO, Verdant Springs), Liam Rivers (Platform Eng), Noah Kim (Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Verdant Springs' time-to-first-token needs, security/compliance constraints, and decide between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC/on‑prem. Customer wants clear path from PLG/self-serve credits to a pilot, and fast perf numbers to validate latency and cost.

Topics covered:
- Quickstart / free credits / time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations
- Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC tradeoffs
- Security controls: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Benchmarking plan: models, sequence lengths, concurrency targets
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Eliot who's our solutions engineer. Um, quick roll call?
00:07 Maya Ortiz: Hey Jordan, Maya here. CTO at Verdant Springs.
00:09 Liam Rivers: Liam, platform eng.
00:10 Noah Kim: Noah, security. Morning.
00:12 Eliot Zhang: Hey all.
00:15 Jordan Meyers: Great. The goal for today is to understand your stack, what "time to first token" looks like for you, and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated, or a Private deployment makes sense given your constraints. Also we'll talk free credits and a quick onramp so you can hit that TTFT quickly.
00:28 Maya Ortiz: Yep, we're primarily evaluating a hosted vendor for initial MVP, but our procurement and security folks will need details if we move to reserved capacity or a private plane, on prem. We want to know: how long to go from sign-up to real traffic? And what the costs look like.
00:40 Jordan Meyers: Totally. Quick question — current stack? Are you cloud-native? Any regulatory constraints or residency needs?
00:46 Liam Rivers: We're on AWS across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. No strict residency yet but we do have PHI-ish internal data for a subset of features, so security is important. We prefer VPC connectivity for anything that touches production data.
01:00 Noah Kim: From security, SOC 2 is a must for vendors; we also use SAML SSO, and we have to integrate customer keys into our KMS eventually. Audit trails and RBAC are mandatory.
01:12 Eliot Zhang: That's straightforward — Redwood supports SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For VPC we have Private deployments and also a Dedicated offering with VPC peering options. The Hosted API is easiest for TTFT but if you need strict network isolation we can discuss Private.
01:28 Maya Ortiz: How fast is "easy"? I mean, from a dev's perspective, sign-up to a test request, what's realistic?
01:34 Jordan Meyers: For PLG/self-serve, typical is under an hour to make a first call: sign up, API key, quickstart SDK, and sample prompt. We'll also provision free credits — usually we start with a 50K token credit bundle for early evaluation, can be sized up.
01:49 Liam Rivers: Under an hour sounds great. But for our security folks, they want to know the minimal uplift to run a pilot in our VPC.
01:55 Eliot Zhang: For a Private VPC, the setup is more involved — networking and provisioning might take a couple of weeks, depending on Egress rules and KMS handshakes. Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering is often a middle ground: predictable throughput, SLOs, and faster provisioning than full private control plane.
02:13 Maya Ortiz: What's the latency delta between Hosted and Dedicated? We expect sub-400ms for single-turn chat on a 13B-ish model.
02:22 Eliot Zhang: Good question. Host ed API on the same region typically gives latencies in the 200–500ms range for 4–8 token prompts on optimized models; depends on model size. Dedicated with reserved GPUs and tuned batching can reduce tails — so you might see median improvements of 20–40ms and better P95 if you pin a model variant and tune batch windows. Private on-prem can be the lowest latency if you colocate, but higher ops overhead.
02:45 Noah Kim: Is there a quantization option? We prefer using int8 or 4-bit for cost reasons but need to know about accuracy tradeoffs.
02:52 Eliot Zhang: Yes — our runtime supports quantized variants. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations slicing by workload. We can serve quantized models that are Redwood-verified with noted quality deltas; we usually run a small eval suite to validate loss in your prompts.
03:08 Liam Rivers: Okay, workflows — we want to roll from PLG into a pilot where we ramp to 100 rps for inference during peak. Any blockers?
03:16 Eliot Zhang: Target throughput of 100 rps is achievable with Dedicated or a scaled Hosted plan; for Hosted you'll want to talk to AE for burst and quota increases. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so you get predictable throughput. We'll need to size based on model, sequence length, batchability.
03:31 Maya Ortiz: On procurement timeline — if pilot looks good, we're hoping to be in pilot in 3–4 weeks. Is that doable?
03:36 Jordan Meyers: Yes, for a Hosted-first pilot we can get you started immediately with credits. For Dedicated/reserved pilot we'd start sizing and can usually bring up capacity in 2–4 weeks depending on exact requirements. Private VPC runs longer.
03:48 Liam Rivers: For the evaluation we'll need a simple perf benchmark: 1) 3B open model for baseline, 2) 13B tuned for parity, 3) a 70B for heavy lift — sequences up to 1024 tokens, concurrent 50–100, P95 latency target <600ms for 70B, <350ms for 13B. Could Redwood run that or give us tooling?
04:07 Eliot Zhang: We have a benchmark playbook and scripts we can share. We also offer to run a controlled benchmark against our hosted infra with your prompt set. We'll need sample prompts and an account to provision credit.
04:19 Maya Ortiz: Great. Security questions: where are logs stored? Who has access? How do you handle customer-managed keys?
04:26 Eliot Zhang: Audit logs are available in the Console with retention options; we also stream audit logs to customer S3 or Splunk on request for enterprise plans. For KMS, we support customer‑managed keys (bring-your-own KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated options; Hosted has Redwood-managed keys but we can offer envelope encryption and strict access controls.
04:47 Noah Kim: And SSO?
04:49 Jordan Meyers: SSO via SAML/Okta is standard, plus we provide RBAC at route and token level. We'll attach role mappings for developers vs ops vs auditors.
04:58 Noah Kim: Perfect. Any certifications besides SOC 2? ISO is in roadmap, but SOC 2 is current.
05:03 Eliot Zhang: Yep. SOC 2 Type II report available for enterprise review.

[-- brief cross talk about onboarding docs and links --]

05:20 Jordan Meyers: I want to call out the TTFT playbook: sign up for self-serve, drop in the SDK snippet, call text generation or embeddings endpoints — you'll have a sample app with webhooks and streaming responses. Most teams see first meaningful response in 20–45 minutes including integration.
05:36 Liam Rivers: Does streaming add latency? We care about perceived response time in-app.
05:40 Eliot Zhang: Streaming cost is about the same per token; perceived latency can be improved because the first tokens arrive earlier. For chat UIs streaming helps a lot.
05:48 Maya Ortiz: Pricing — can you send an apples-to-apples cost comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? We want to present to CFO.
05:56 Jordan Meyers: Absolutely — I'll send a matrix showing unit economics, reservation discounts, and typical CPU/GPU sizing assumptions. For Dedicated we show committed spend vs per-token costs.
06:06 Maya Ortiz: Do you support model pinning and rollouts? We may need canary testing for new model variants.
06:11 Eliot Zhang: Yes — rollouts and A/B canary policies are built into the Console; automatic fallback to smaller variants is supported for graceful degradation.
06:20 Maya Ortiz: For the pilot, what are common failure modes? We need to know SLAs and degrade patterns.
06:25 Eliot Zhang: Common failures: GPU OOMs for large batch sizes — our autoscaler and preflight can detect that. Also network hiccups — we have retries and fallback to a compatible model variant. For Hosted we publish uptime SLOs and error rate dashboards; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and custom alerting.

08:05 Speaker 1: [inaudible] I think we should also consider data retention policies, we have to purge PII after 90 days.
08:12 Eliot Zhang: We have retention controls and you can set automatic purges. Also redaction hooks for prompt preprocessing if you want to scrub PII client-side.

09:02 Maya Ortiz: One more on compliance — can we get a temporary access pass to the SOC 2 report and sample contracts? That's essential before procurement pushes forward.
09:10 Jordan Meyers: Yes, I'll include the SOC 2 report and our standard DPA in the doc package.

10:18 Liam Rivers: On the technical side, any special VM images or agents needed for VPC peering?
10:23 Eliot Zhang: No agents for peering — we do secure egress/ingress via peering and a small VPN handshake. For on‑prem private deployments there is an appliance-ish container bundle, but we handle most heavy lifting.

12:00 Noah Kim: For KMS keys — can we rotate keys on our cadence?
12:04 Eliot Zhang: Yes. Customer-managed keys follow your rotation schedule; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with rotation hooks.

13:15 Maya Ortiz: Let's talk timeline and success criteria. For us success is: 1) TTFT under an hour to first dev calls, 2) pilot demonstrating <350ms median on the 13B for our average prompts, 3) security sign-off with SOC 2 and KMS integration. 4) a go/no-go decision within 4 weeks.
13:36 Jordan Meyers: That's achievable. We'll provision credits and a sandbox account today, send the benchmark playbook, and coordinate a deep technical session for the infra folks next week.

15:05 Liam Rivers: A question on data residency — if we start in us-east but later need eu-west, can we route by policy or do we need a new org?
15:13 Eliot Zhang: We support multi-region routing. Requests can be routed by region/tenant/policy with automatic fallback; you can pin workloads to regions.

17:22 Maya Ortiz: Do you have any examples of customers in regulated verticals that started Hosted then moved to Dedicated? Would be helpful to see a short case study.
17:30 Jordan Meyers: Yes — we've got a case with a healthtech customer that started self-serve and then moved to Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS. I'll include a redacted case study in the packet.

19:01 Noah Kim: On observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route? We want to attribute costs to product teams.
19:08 Eliot Zhang: Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can tag requests so costs are attributable.

21:00 Maya Ortiz: What about model updates — how do you ensure no quality regressions on new releases?
21:06 Eliot Zhang: We tie regressions to eval sets and run pre-deploy checks. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and substitution with rollback policies if quality drops.

24:00 Liam Rivers: For the benchmark, do you need us to disable rate limits? Our prod traffic pattern is bursty.
24:07 Eliot Zhang: We'll work with you to simulate bursts; for Hosted we'll request temporary quota increases during the test. For Dedicated capacity we size for peak concurrency.

26:10 Maya Ortiz: Cost sensitivity — CFO will ask: what's the break-even point between Hosted and Dedicated?
26:17 Jordan Meyers: We'll include a cost model. Usually if you have sustained high QPS (requests per second) and large token volumes, Dedicated becomes cheaper after reservation discounts. We can run a breakeven calc with your expected monthly tokens.

29:13 Liam Rivers: Anything else?
29:17 Jordan Meyers: A couple of practical next steps: I'll send the quickstart link and provision the trial credits; Eliot will send the benchmark repo and sample prompts; Maya you mentioned a compliance checklist — if you share that we'll map items to our controls.
29:31 Maya Ortiz: We'll send the checklist by EOD tomorrow.

31:12 Noah Kim: One minor note — we need to ensure that logs and prompts with PHI are never stored or are encrypted at rest with customer-controlled keys. Confirm?
31:21 Eliot Zhang: Confirm — for Dedicated/Private we can ensure customer-controlled KMS and restrict log storage. Hosted has options for streaming logs to your account and short retention. We'll document exact controls in the DPA.

33:40 Jordan Meyers: Recap: 1) Provision 50K credits and create trial org 2) Share SOC 2 and DPA, pricing matrix 3) Benchmark playbook from Eliot 4) Schedule infra deep-dive for 2027-01-28 — does that date work?
33:58 Maya Ortiz: 2027-01-28 works for us.
34:02 Liam Rivers: Works.
34:04 Noah Kim: Works.

35:00 Jordan Meyers: Great — I'll push notes and the packet after this meeting. Any final questions?
35:08 Maya Ortiz: No, thanks. Appreciate the clarity.
35:11 Eliot Zhang: Thanks everyone.
35:13 Speaker 2: [crosstalk] Bye.

36:00 End of meeting.
